business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Supply of Drummed and Bagged Penetration Grade Bitumen

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil law rooted in the French/Napoleonic codification, with residual Sharia-derived principles in commercial and personal status matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1975, extended by the UK-Egypt Investment Treaty 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 221 of 1951 on Commercial Registers; Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint-Stock Companies, Limited Partnerships and Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 as amended by Law No. 75 of 2018; Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019; GAFI Beneficial Ownership Identification and Record-Keeping Instructions (including GAFI Form No. 9 under the Investment Law); Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Instructions; Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) implementing rules and red flag guidelines

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of parent entity (foreign company register extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the competent Egyptian consulate in the parent jurisdiction; Hague Apostille is not accepted because Egypt is not a Contracting State to the 1961 Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency applying to the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent jurisdiction's competent corporate registry or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the competent Egyptian consulate; accompanied by a sworn Arabic translation certified before the Egyptian Egyptian Due Diligence Officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the Egyptian incorporation signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity's board of directors / notarial authority in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization plus notarized Arabic translation; apostille not recognized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification dossier (certified passport copies, source of funds declaration, bank reference letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution and notary in the jurisdiction of residence of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the nearest Egyptian consular post and sworn Arabic translation; original bank letter must carry authorized signature verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HM Treasury consolidated list, Arab Republic of Egypt's terrorism designation lists published in the Official Gazette, and GAFI's internal ineligibility checks. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, documented source of funds, senior management approval, and verification of business justification. Screening results and adverse media searches must be retained in the AML/CFT file and produced upon EMLCU inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Egyptian Companies and Investment Portal (InvestInEgypt.gov.eg / GAFI Irada Online System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names for Egyptian LLCs must contain a distinctive Arabic name as a primary registered name for the local Commercial Register, with an optional English transliteration for banking and trade use. The Arabic name must be consistent with tariff law principles of distinctive character and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered mark or company name. Latin-script names are permitted as a secondary name but cannot omit the statutory suffix 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company' in either the Arabic or English version.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misr/Egypt in a manner suggesting state affiliation
words implying public concession or sovereign authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection or refusal notice, the applicant or authorized counsel shall file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Dispute Resolution and Investment Complaints Committee no later than 30 days from the date of refusal, stating the conflict between the proposed name and the registry's distinctiveness criteria. The Committee issues a reasoned decision within 15 business days; further non-final registry decisions may be contested before the Economic Administrative Court under the provisions of Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. The appeal file must include a copy of the refused clearance note, the Arabic-language proposed name, and evidence of prior registration or search differences.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office may be established at a licensed commercial agent, law firm, or an approved GAFI business centre in Cairo or a governorate service office, subject to the provision of a physical address for service. For an ISIC 4661 bitumen wholesaling and containerized asphalt logistics undertaking, the authority will generally accept a virtual head office for administrative and registration purposes, but a commercial substance argument requires evidence of bank accounts, management function, trade documentation, and tax DW payments in Egypt. If the activity involves bonded storage or physical warehousing of bitumen drums, a separate operating address and environmental clearance may be required, making a pure virtual office insufficient for that operating layer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. For a containerized bitumen trading entity operating under ISIC 4661, the estimated probability of an unannounced GAFI, Commercial Registry, or tax enforcement inspection is 15% to 20% per year, primarily triggered by customs import volume, VAT desk audits, and sudden registration address changes. Warehousing or tank storage locations are subject to additional environmental and safety inspections at higher probability.

stage_2.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment
stage_2.classification_tier: Category B (List 2 of Law 4/1994 Executive Regulations): Environmental Screening and Site-Specific Impact Review required before operation; operator must obtain an environmental review certificate; if storage capacity exceeds 10,000 tonnes, Category C (List 3) may trigger a Full EIA Report.
stage_2.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Executive Regulations of Law No. 4/1994 as amended and Ministerial Decree 92/2014 for wastewater discharge to sewer (BOD ≤ 60 mg/l, COD ≤ 100 mg/l, oil & grease ≤ 15 mg/l); air emission limits under Article 42 of Law 4/1994 and EEAA ambient standards for PM10 and NOx; fugitive volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions minimized through closed drumming, vapor recovery, and regular ambient air monitoring; hazardous waste handling under a manifest/waste tracking system and licensed disposal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA, مصلحة الضرائب المصرية), Ministry of Finance; unified taxpayer digital portal https://www.eta.gov.eg (e-filing, e-invoice, e-receipt); customs and foreign-trade single window operated with the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) at https://www.nafeza.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must (i) incorporate before the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) one-stop shop, obtain the Commercial Registration extract, and publish the statutory notice; (ii) apply to ETA for the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax card within 30 days of commencing activity, submitting the LLC contractual documents, commercial registration certificate, power of attorney, authorized officer identity documents, registered address/lease, and board resolution; (iii) obtain a separate VAT registration code once annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 (or voluntarily above EGP 150,000); (iv) register in the NAFEZA single window and the GOEIC exporter/importer register for foreign-trade and customs codes. A non-resident exporter without an Egyptian establishment is not required to obtain an Egyptian TIN solely for zero-rated containerized export sales, but importers/buyers in Egypt must be VAT-registered to clear goods through customs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – an Egyptian LLC is a tax-resident juridical entity taxed at entity level on worldwide income at the standard 22.5% corporate income tax rate (Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 26/2020 and consolidated for income/stamp/real-estate taxes under Unified Tax Law 67/2023). No pass-through, tax-transparent, or check-the-box status is recognized under Egyptian law; non-resident shareholders are taxed only on Egypt-source income, with final withholding on dividends. A pure wholesale trading LLC situated outside a licensed free zone or Suez Canal Economic Zone project is assessed under the ordinary resident company regime; zone-located logistics projects may elect special investment-law incentives.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a US-style check-the-box or entity-classification election; tax classification follows legal form and place of incorporation/effective management. Available statutory and administrative elections include: (i) selection of a non-calendar fiscal year approved by ETA; (ii) voluntary VAT registration where annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 150,000 but remain below the EGP 500,000 mandatory threshold; (iii) election between investment-law incentives and the ordinary tax regime for free-zone/SCZone-licensed projects; (iv) election of monthly refund set-off against output VAT rather than cash refunds. Hybrid mismatch consequences follow the OECD BEPS-aligned provisions in the unified tax law without discretionary entity-level elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3/2020 and Law No. 41/2022, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority; import VAT and customs duties under Customs Law No. 207/2020 are collected through the NAFEZA single window.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 per annum of taxable supplies (mandatory registration within 30 days); voluntary registration is available where annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 150,000. Non-resident suppliers have no general de minimis for B2C supplies and imported B2B services are subject to reverse-charge/withholding VAT collected by the Egyptian buyer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipts apply to all VAT-registered taxpayers: tax invoices must be issued exclusively through ETA-approved channels, either the taxpayer web portal or an ERP/API integration submitting XML/JSON documents with the taxpayer's digital signature and embedded QR code (E-Invoice/E-Receipt system, phased rollout completed by 2023). The ETA validates each document in near real time and issues a submission/approval reference; invoices failing validation are treated as not issued and attract administrative fines. For exports, the e-invoice must be matched with the NAFEZA/ACID customs declaration and the cargo release record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Egypt, including containerized drummed/bagged penetration-grade bitumen, qualify for the 0% VAT rate where: (i) title passes to the non-resident buyer; (ii) the goods are removed from Egypt under customs control within the statutory export period (generally 90 days from the export tax invoice date under the VAT Law and its executive regulations); (iii) the exporter retains a complete documentary file proving customs exit, foreign payment, and repatriation of proceeds. Services directly related to the export of goods, including ocean freight, cargo handling, port services, and offshore storage, together with services supplied to non-resident recipients and consumed wholly outside Egypt, are also zero-rated. Domestic sales, sales to Egyptian intermediaries for resale within Egypt, and any quantity lost or diverted in local circulation remain taxable at 14%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration via NAFEZA (ACID-linked, with customs release certificate and export declaration number)
ETA-validated e-invoice and packing list containing the invoice submission reference and QR code
Export Contract / sale invoice (SC) evidencing the foreign buyer and Incoterms
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill evidencing loading from an Egyptian port and foreign destination
Certificate of origin, product specification sheets, and safety data sheets for bitumen as required by customs/GOEIC
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank MT103 confirmation showing hard-currency export proceeds credited to an Egyptian bank account
Container/terminal receipt or weight certificate confirming the goods left the Egyptian customs territory within the permitted window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The zero-rating is provisional until the complete export and FX file is substantiated. If any required customs, logistics, or repatriation document is missing, inconsistent, or late, ETA reclassifies the supply as a domestic taxable transaction, assesses VAT at 14%, imposes monthly delay fines and interest in accordance with the VAT Law and Unified Tax Law 67/2023 execution rules, and retroactively reverses any refund or input-tax offset (clawback) associated with the disallowed export. Deliberate fabrication of export declarations, circular export-import schemes, over-invoicing for foreign-currency leakage, or failure to repatriate proceeds within the CBE-prescribed period attract criminal evasion penalties, including imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to EGP 10,000,000, customs penalties under Law 207/2020, Central Bank of Egypt foreign-exchange sanctions, and suspension or removal of the taxpayer's GOEIC/NAFEZA exporter registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with comprehensive capital controls enforced by the Central Bank of Egypt. Current account transactions, including trade settlements and approved profit remittances, are generally convertible upon submission of supporting documentation. Capital account transactions, such as equity injections and intercompany loans, require prior CBE approval and are subject to quantitative limits and documentation verification. Profit remittance hurdles include mandatory tax clearance, compliance with anti-avoidance provisions, and potential delays for amounts exceeding specified thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export receipts denominated in foreign currency must be surrendered to an authorized Egyptian bank within six months of collection. Surrender is mandatory at 100% of the realized foreign exchange value, converted to Egyptian Pounds at the prevailing official CBE rate. Non-compliance triggers administrative penalties, potential license suspension, and restrictions on future export financing facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institution cross-border viability is severely constrained under CBE regulations. Offshore digital EMIs require mandatory partnerships with CBE-licensed Egyptian banks for FX custody and settlement services. Legal constraints include full compliance with the Central Bank of Egypt's fintech licensing framework, AML/CFT obligations, and prohibition on direct handling of foreign currency by unlicensed entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and authorized signatories is mandatory for KYC interviews and corporate account opening for Egyptian LLCs, particularly where non-resident beneficial owners are involved. Remote digital KYC is permitted only for low-value operational accounts; cross-border trade finance and FX activities require in-person verification or notarized power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of beneficial ownership, corporate organigram, source of wealth documentation, and declaration of ultimate beneficial owners exceeding 25% stake
Commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and underlying trade agreement demonstrating legitimate bitumen asphalt logistics activity
Board resolution authorizing injection, valuation report, and proof of legitimate equity contribution from foreign parent or investor

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are processed via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION'. All transactions require CBE prior approval for amounts exceeding EGP 100,000 equivalent, accompanied by board resolutions, investment agreements, and valuation reports. Verification includes matching against registered capital in the commercial register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for payments and Commercial Letters of Credit for larger settlements. All transactions must incorporate CBE-approved purpose codes such as 'TRADE' or 'IMPORT PAYMENT' and be supported by underlying commercial documents including invoices and delivery receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with financial statements and auditor documentation where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year company, generally by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, tax interest, assessment risk, and enforcement under the Income Tax Law; no fixed annual tax-return deadline automatically triggers administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, auditor report, and ordinary general meeting approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company partners; filings or submissions to GAFI and the Commercial Registry where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual process after financial year-end; the ordinary general meeting should approve the accounts within the statutory period applicable to the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential Companies Law penalties, director and manager liability, refusal or delay of related registry actions, and regulatory enforcement; no universal automatic strike-off date applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry information and company data renewal or amendment filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No universal annual franchise-return deadline; amendments to registered particulars should be filed promptly within the applicable statutory period, and registry renewals follow the validity period stated on the relevant certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, inability to complete certain corporate or banking transactions, and possible cancellation or strike-off following notices and applicable legal procedures; no fixed automatic annual strike-off timeline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review of partners, managers, beneficial ownership, registered address, and corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; GAFI, Commercial Registry, and competent authorities upon filing or request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Complete at least annually and update the relevant authority promptly after any change in ownership, management, address, or beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update information may result in AML/CFT sanctions, Companies Law penalties, registry restrictions, and enhanced regulatory scrutiny

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Egyptian LLCs generally require appointment of a licensed auditor and annual audit under the Companies Law; additional audited-financial-statement requirements may apply based on statutory capital, turnover, tax, sector, or regulatory criteria. No universal small-company exemption should be assumed without confirming current Egyptian rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards, with IFRS-based principles as incorporated into the Egyptian framework; tax filings must comply with Egyptian tax legislation and Egyptian Tax Authority requirements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Conduct an annual written confirmation that partner interests, transfers, control rights, managers, and beneficial owners remain unchanged. Record all transfers in the partners register and supporting corporate documents, and file required amendments with GAFI or the Commercial Registry promptly after a change. There is no generally applicable standalone annual UBO declaration replacing change-based updates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Accounting books and supporting financial records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 500-2,000 per year, excluding governmental filing charges, translations, notarization, and special licensing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-8,000 per year for a small operating LLC; higher fees may apply for inventory, imports, related-party transactions, multiple branches, or complex consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, eligible projects in certain sectors or geographic zones may receive a 50% reduction of the income tax payable on profits for a period not exceeding 7 years, subject to Cabinet approval and compliance with the investment map. Wholesale bitumen trading is generally not automatically eligible; no unrestricted tax holiday applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 30 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (e-tax.gov.eg); mandatory for all resident companies including LLCs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory quarterly advance income tax payments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from sales and services (drummed and bagged bitumen sales, containerized supply contracts, ancillary logistics income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders report their distributive share only at withholding level; the LLC must report all Egyptian-source revenue in EGP at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: CIF cost of imported bitumen, container freight, inland freight, customs duties, handling and demurrage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party import invoices must be substantiated with bills of lading, customs declarations, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: warehousing, port storage, insurance, administrative salaries, professional fees, and other deductible overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any head-office cost allocation from a foreign parent must satisfy the benefit test and be supported by records kept in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before statutory deductions and loss carryforward (reconciliation between accounting net profit and tax accounting adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC must compute and document an arm's length net margin consistent with wholesale distribution benchmarks; foreign participants may not unilaterally reallocate profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, advance payments, and prepaid CIT instalments (quarterly advances based on prior-year tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are allowed only under the applicable DTA or Egyptian foreign tax credit rules; no credit for foreign shareholder-level taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at 22.5% on the taxable base after all statutory deductions and offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax assessed at 22.5% is in addition to the 10% dividend WHT on distributions to foreign shareholders; both liabilities must be separately declared and paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment attracts a monthly surcharge of 2% of the net tax due for each month or part thereof, capped at 50% of the tax; fixed non-compliance fines may range from EGP 1,000 to EGP 5,000; intentional non-filing is subject to criminal prosecution under Law No. 91 of 2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under Article 56 of Law No. 91 of 2005 on dividends distributed by an Egyptian resident company to a non-resident shareholder; treaty relief may reduce this rate depending on the reciprocal DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficiary must submit to the ETA a treaty relief application (Form No. 61), a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, proof of beneficial ownership, and the distribution resolution. The Egyptian payer must retain the approved documentation to apply the reduced DTA withholding rate at source; a refund can be claimed if excess WHT was withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic WHT is 20% for IP royalties and 20% for debt interest paid to non-residents. Under most Egyptian double tax agreements, rates are commonly reduced to 10%-15% for interest and 10%-15% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and submission of a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 15,000,000 annual related-party transaction value per counterparty triggers mandatory Local File; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 1,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). However, Egyptian tax authorities apply substance-over-form, GAAR, and beneficial ownership principles; the bitumen trading LLC must maintain physical office/warehouse presence, staff, logistics records, and board decisions in Egypt to secure tax residency and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying purchase invoices for containerized bitumen, understating box 1 revenues, or generating fictitious offsetting expenses to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine equal to 50%-200% of the evaded tax, imprisonment for up to 5 years, asset seizure, and mandatory re-assessment under Law No. 91 of 2005 Articles 133-138.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; travel bans, passport restrictions, disqualification from management, and criminal imprisonment apply to those filing false returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a re-invoicing shell with no physical presence, staff, warehouse, or decision-making in Egypt, using DTA benefits while performing business in a no-tax or conduit jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, disregard of separate legal personality, application of the Egyptian GAAR, a 50% deficiency penalty on the additional tax, and possible cancellation of tax registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing: shareholders and directors may be personally assessed for the whole corporate tax debt, subjected to travel bans, and criminally prosecuted for fraud if the shell arrangement is considered a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany purchase prices for bitumen are marked up more than 20% above arm's length, or the LLC fails to file the TP disclosure and Local File while exceeding the EGP 15 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-characterizes the profit at the arm's length level, imposes a TP adjustment penalty of up to 100% of the additional tax, plus a 2% per month late-payment surcharge on the adjusted tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chief financial officer and tax directors can be held personally liable; civil restitution for lost tax, director disqualification, and criminal liability for knowingly submitting incorrect TP documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving cash or laundering proceeds through over/under-invoicing of containerized bitumen, using shell intermediaries, or transacting with sanctioned or politically exposed counterparties without AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80 of 2002 and its amendments, imprisonment up to 15 years, a fine equal to at least twice the value of the laundered funds, freezing of bank accounts and cargo, and confiscation of the bitumen inventory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in or negligently facilitating money laundering are subject to personal asset forfeiture, travel bans, international extradition, and imprisonment; corporate banking privileges are suspended.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders without deducting the 10% WHT, or applying a treaty rate without a TRC and beneficial ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monthly 2% delay penalty up to 50% of the unpaid WHT, fixed deficiency fines of EGP 1,000-5,000, enforced collection via bank attachment, and criminal prosecution for collection evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors remain personally liable for the withheld tax not remitted, with joint liability for restitution; travel bans and attachment of personal assets are common enforcement measures.
